name: Lying Plate Neck Curl
aliases: Lying Face Up Plate Neck Resistance
why: Trains the front of the neck.
setup: Lie face up on a bench, head and neck off the end.
Light plate on your forehead over a towel, both hands on it.
form: Bring your chin to your chest.
Lower your head back to level.
tips: Start very light and add weight slowly.
avoid: Heavy weight or reps to failure.

preferred.why: Direct front-of-neck work: the neck grows only when trained directly.

name: Lying Plate Neck Extension
aliases: Lying Face Down Plate Neck Resistance
why: Trains the back of the neck.
setup: Lie face down on a bench, head and neck off the end.
Light plate on the back of your head over a towel, hands on it. Chin toward your chest.
form: Lift your head until you look straight ahead.
Lower until your chin nears your chest.
tips: Start very light and add weight slowly.
avoid: Heavy weight or reps to failure.

name: Neck Harness Extension
why: Back-of-neck work that is easy to load.
setup: Sit on a bench edge, lean forward, hands on your knees.
Harness on your head, weight hanging, chin toward your chest.
form: Lift your head until you look forward.
Lower until your chin nears your chest.
tips: Start very light and add weight slowly.
avoid: Leaning your body back to lift.

preferred.why: Easiest way to load the back of the neck; head extension training grew those muscles in a 12-week trial.

name: Machine Neck Flexion
why: Front-of-neck work on a 4-way neck machine.
setup: Sit facing the pad, forehead against it.
Torso still, hands on the handles.
form: Bring your chin toward your chest.
tips: Start very light and add weight slowly.
avoid: Heavy weight or reps to failure.

name: Machine Neck Extension
why: Back-of-neck work on a 4-way neck machine.
setup: Sit facing away, back of your head on the pad, chin slightly down.
Torso still, hands on the handles.
form: Push your head back until you look slightly up.
tips: Start very light and add weight slowly.
avoid: Heavy weight or reps to failure.
rangeOfMotion: Chin slightly down → looking slightly up

name: Lying Plate Neck Side Raise
why: Trains the sides of the neck.
setup: Lie on your side on a bench, head and neck off the end.
Light plate on the side of your head over a towel, top hand on it.
form: Lift your ear toward your top shoulder.
Lower to a light stretch; switch sides.
tips: Start very light and add weight slowly.
avoid: Heavy weight or reps to failure.
rangeOfMotion: Head tilted down → ear toward the top shoulder

name: Machine Neck Side Bend
why: Side-of-neck work on a 4-way neck machine.
setup: Sit side-on, side of your head on the pad, head upright.
Torso still, hands on the handles.
form: Bend your ear toward your shoulder.
tips: Start very light and add weight slowly.
avoid: Heavy weight or reps to failure.
rangeOfMotion: Head upright → ear toward the shoulder
